title: Power Rankings: Cavs lose No. 1 spot to Lakers
heading: 2009-10 Power Rankings: Week 17
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: As ridiculously hot as Utah has been for the past six weeks, L.A.'s win in Salt Lake City without Kobe before the All-Star Game is even more impressive than we thought. It's a deserved return to the rankings summit.

rankings.summaryHtml: Rest assured that the Cavs will eventually get Big Z back without much league interference. I'm pretty sure their mojo will be back soon, too, because a no-brainer trade and Mo Williams' return have to be positives.

rankings.summaryHtml: A trade for a vet would have been nice and ''Durantula'' still doesn't work for me as a nickname, but there isn't much else here to protest. Not when OKC is a tidy 20-8 during Durant's streak of consecutive 25-point games.

rankings.summaryHtml: The race for the No. 2 seed in the West, for so long a two-teamer between Denver and Dallas, is suddenly a four-team jumble thanks to the rise of Utah and OKC. Which is another reason the Mavs' trade was so timely.
